os-10-12.alt: A three-panel diagram of how muscle remakes ATP. Top panel: in resting muscle, ATP and creatine combine to form creatine phosphate and ADP; in active muscle, the enzyme creatine kinase moves the phosphate from creatine phosphate back to ADP, giving creatine and ATP for contraction. Middle panel: glucose from the blood and from muscle glycogen enters glycolysis, which yields 2 ATP and 2 pyruvate; with oxygen, pyruvate goes on to aerobic respiration, and without it, it leaves as lactic acid to the blood. Bottom panel: glucose from the blood, pyruvic acid and fatty acids enter a mitochondrion, which uses oxygen to make many ATP, heat, carbon dioxide and water.
